title: Approval middleware and minimal audit PRD (rough)
summary: Rough product requirements for a lightweight approval middleware that sits between the control plane and customer-managed networking to provide short-lived approval windows, compact audit receipts, and an operator-friendly UX. Goal: enable safe, low-bandwidth approvals and forensic evidence for private deployments without requiring full heavy-weight audit pipelines inside customer networks.
goals: 1) Provide a minimal approval path that generates cryptographically linkable receipts customers can archive. 2) Keep audit payload small (target median < 2KB per approval) to support low-bandwidth sites. 3) Offer configurable retention windows and automated pruning hooks so customers can meet retention policies without storing everything indefinitely. 4) Expose a streamlined operator UX for approving network changes with clear end-to-end evidence. 5) Define SLA/timeout behaviors for approval windows to avoid blocking customers' on-call flows.
scope: In-scope: middleware API and lightweight evidence envelope format, operator approval flow patterns (canary, immediate, batched), retention/pruning controls surfaced in the console and via API, telemetry for approval latency and evidence size. Out-of-scope: full SIEM integrations (will provide export hooks), long-term cold storage solutions, and policy enforcement inside customer firewalls (middleware assumes minimal outbound connectivity to Redwood).
non_goals: We will not attempt to replicate an enterprise SIEM; we are not building a full evidence archival service. This PRD also does not include detailed cryptographic HSM integration (KMS integration is documented elsewhere). We are not changing the core control-plane approval authorization model in this work.
requirements:
Functional requirements:
- FR1: Middleware must accept approval requests via REST and gRPC and return a short approval token and a compact evidence receipt.
- FR2: Evidence receipt contains: approval id, timestamp, actor id, minimal diff of requested config, a small set of signed hashes of related artifacts (no full payloads).
- FR3: Approval windows configurable per-customer (default 10min, min 30s, max 24h).
- FR4: Middleware supports three approval modes: immediate-approve, staged-canary, deferred-batch.
- FR5: Console shows the active approvals list with inline evidence preview and a one-click approve/deny UX for operators.
- FR6: Retention policies: customer-configurable TTL for evidence (e.g., 7d, 30d, 90d) plus a manual-archive endpoint.
- FR7: Pruning API must produce a compact index file (JSON-lines) that proves what was pruned (hash list + range) so customers can retain a searchable metadata layer without full payloads.
Non-functional requirements:
- NFR1: Median evidence size < 2KB; 99th percentile < 16KB.
- NFR2: Approval round-trip latency for immediate-approve < 500ms under normal conditions.
- NFR3: Middleware must operate with intermittent connectivity — queue approval requests locally and retry, with exposed status.
- NFR4: Availability target for middleware control-plane endpoints: 99.9% monthly for Dedicated customers; 99.5% for standard private.
- NFR5: Audit receipts cryptographically signed with a Redwood key and optionally customer-signed stamp (when key-swivel is configured).
ux_flow:
Operator flow (console):
1) Operator clicks 'Propose change' from customer network page.
2) Change payload is diffed client-side; middleware receives only compact diff + metadata.
3) UI shows proposed change, minimal evidence snapshot, and two buttons: Approve / Request more info.
4) Approve triggers immediate-approve mode or opens canary configuration modal.
5) On approve, middleware returns evidence receipt with link to download the signed proof.
6) If no response within approval window, middleware either auto-denies or auto-escalates per customer policy.
Edge cases: network partition — operator can mark approval as 'queued' and the middleware will attach a connectivity signature once it can reach Redwood.
telemetry_and_metrics: Minimum telemetry: total approvals per-customer per-hour, median approval latency, evidence size distribution, approvals auto-denied due to timeout, queued approvals count, prune operations per-day, prune bytes reclaimed. Export hooks: metrics export to customer Prometheus push gateway or to our metrics export endpoint. Sampling: default 1.0 for errors, 0.1 for successful approvals for payload-level telemetry to limit PII exposure.
security_and_privacy: Design assumptions: middleware should never persist full configuration payloads longer than necessary unless customer opts in. Evidence receipts are minimized and hashed; any personally identifiable fields must be removed or tokenized before inclusion. Encrypt evidence at rest using customer KMS when available. Provide a 'redact' option for operators to strip fields from receipts. Provide an attestation header for proofs generated during network-limited scenarios so we can show later that a request was accepted while offline.
retention_and_pruning: Retention model: per-customer TTL + manual archive. Pruning strategy: run compactify job that replaces detailed evidence blobs older than TTL with a compact index entry: {approval_id, timestamp, actor_hash, payload_hash, prune_range_id}. Customers can optionally ship full archived blobs to their own S3 by providing a signed upload endpoint. Pruning job must produce a signed compact-index file and a tamper-evident manifest so legal/forensics teams can rely on it.
sla_and_approval_window_policies: Default policy: 10 minute approval window for manual operations; auto-deny after window if policy is 'strict'. Customers can set policy to 'escalate' which triggers an on-call SMS/Slack webhook and extends window by configured jitter. For scheduled bulk operations, allow a batch window with rolling canaries (percent + time). Define SLOs: mean time to evidence issuance after approve < 250ms, SLA for acknowledgment of queued approvals when connectivity returns < 60s.
implementation_notes:
- Prototype evidence envelope using CBOR-minified JSON to hit size targets.
- Use an incremental Merkle hash chain per-customer for compact proofing (store only roots in control plane).
- Build a small SDK helper for customer operators to generate compact diffs client-side.
- Hook pruning jobs into existing telemetry/retention pipeline to reuse quota accounting.
- Provide a 'safe-mode' operator flag that keeps full blobs for 30 days even if TTL is shorter, for customers onboarding from legacy systems.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Customers may expect full payloads for forensic investigations. Mitigation: provide clear guidance and an optional 'archive-on-approve' flag that pushes full payloads to customer-owned storage.
Risk: Size targets may be missed with complex diffs. Mitigation: server-side diff normalization and max-diff-size rejection with operator guidance.
Risk: Compliance teams require longer retention. Mitigation: TTL is configurable; integrate export hooks to third-party archives.
open_questions:
1) Legal: is a compact-index + signed manifest sufficient for GDPR/PCI audits in target customers? Who to consult?
2) UX: do security teams want inline redaction controls or a separate redaction request flow?
3) Architecture: shall we require outbound HTTPS from customer operator workstations, or support brokered approval via air-gapped file exchange?
4) Metrics: what is acceptable sampling for successful approvals to avoid capturing sensitive content?
next_steps_and_timeline:
- Feb 2025: spike prototype (evidence envelope + SDK helper) by eng-applied-ml and serving-runtime.
- Mar 2025: UX mockups and small user testing with 3 pilot customers (solutions-eng + customer-success).
- Apr 2025: internal security review and compliance check.
- May 2025: alpha release to Dedicated customers with opt-in archive flag.
- Q3 2025: general availability after telemetry-based thresholds are validated.
